audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] tells the player 'his armor is wasted stats'. Ground Slam deals magic damage based on Malphite's Armor — his armour is his damage. Granite Shield is never mentioned in the content layer at all, and Thunderclap's on-hit aftershocks are named only in passing as 'W (Thunderclap)-empowered autos' with no explanation.
audit.why: Telling a Cho'Gath that Malphite's armour is wasted invites him to walk into an armour-scaling Ground Slam and an on-hit Thunderclap and wonder where the damage came from. Granite Shield absorbs up to 10% of Malphite's maximum health and recharges whenever he goes a few seconds unhit, which is precisely why single pokes never stick and why a committed Rupture-Feral Scream-spikes sequence does. Thunderclap is 10s at rank 1 and turns his attacks into on-hit cone aftershocks, so the correct instruction is to trade after it expires, not into it.
audit.corrected: Say the armour feeds Ground Slam, add Granite Shield's 10% absorb and recharge, and give Thunderclap its 10s window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers score Levels 4-5 and Level 6 as Skill and give First item and 2+ items to Malphite. The packet chart gives Cho'Gath all four, and so does the content prose: 'Now the lane tips your way', 'you out-sustain his Q poke and start winning every extended trade', 'He has no way to scale out of this'. diff also reads EVEN at 6/10 on a 55.62% matchup over 1086 games — the largest sample on the page.
audit.why: Malphite's mirror audit (audits/top/malphite__chogath.json) independently found the same contradiction and wrote in its notes that the chart needed a hand fix, but did not propose it because it believed side/win values fell outside the length band. They are enum fields and exempt, so I am proposing the flip from this side.
audit.corrected: Chart becomes Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath, Cho'Gath with ratings 5, 5, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7; diffRating 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstoppable Force is named in a dozen fields with no cooldown, and no other Malphite number appears anywhere.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100 seconds and 1000 range — one of the longest ultimate cooldowns Cho'Gath faces in top lane, which is what makes 'bait it' genuinely decisive rather than a platitude. Seismic Shard is 8s flat at 625 range and steals move speed rather than merely slowing. Ground Slam is 7s flat. Thunderclap is 10s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Put 130s, 8s, 7s and 10s into cooldowns, dosFull, dontsFull and loading.

audit.whatIsWrong: All three Critical Don'ts have descriptions that belong to other matchups — 'Auto into his W', 'Eat his R knockup' and 'Fall behind in scaling' are each explained with generic Rupture-whiff or burn-your-W text.
audit.why: Every heading here names a real mistake in this lane and none of them is explained.
audit.corrected: Rewrite all three bodies with Thunderclap's 10s, Unstoppable Force's 130s, and Feast's permanent max health.

edits.before: Build AP — Rupture, Feral Scream and Vorpal Spikes are all magic, so his armor is wasted stats
edits.after: Build AP — your whole kit is magic, but his armour isn't wasted: Ground Slam's damage scales off it

edits.before: Levels 2-3 are the danger window, and it's because of your own weakness, not his strength: you're slow, short-ranged, and helpless until Rupture is up, so his Seismic Shard (Q) slow-poke chips you for free. Don't throw Rupture as a poke he can just walk out of — last-hit with Vorpal Spikes (E) and lean on Carnivore's heal-on-kill, eat a little Q damage, and wait. He has no kill pressure and no magic resist here; this is pure chip you heal back the moment your combo comes online.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 are the danger window, and it's your own weakness rather than his strength: you're slow, short-ranged and helpless until Rupture is up, so Seismic Shard (Q) — 8s flat, 625 range, and it steals your move speed — chips you for free. Don't throw Rupture as poke he walks out of; last-hit with Vorpal Spikes (E) and lean on Carnivore's heal-on-kill. Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health and recharges whenever he goes unhit, so a single poke never sticks anyway.

edits.before: Now the lane tips your way. Carnivore's heal-and-mana on every CS plus your Rupture-into-Feral Scream combo turn his Q poke into a sustain you simply out-pace. Bait the Q, then Rupture the knockup into the Feral Scream silence and stack Vorpal Spikes autos — he keeps buying armor, but your damage is all magic and the silence shuts off his Q and W. At 6, Feast is true damage that ignores his entire armor build and answers his only real threat, Unstoppable Force (R): survive the knockup, then execute him.
edits.after: Now the lane tips your way. Carnivore's heal-and-mana on every CS plus your Rupture-into-Feral Scream combo turn his Q poke into chip you simply out-pace. edits.before: This only gets more lopsided. Malphite builds full armor while every tool you own — Rupture, Feral Scream, Vorpal Spikes — deals magic damage his stacked armor never touches, and Feast's true-damage execute deletes him no matter how tanky he gets. The one thing to respect all game is his Unstoppable Force flanking your carries in a teamfight; in the side-lane 1v1 he cannot win. Keep stacking Feast, hold your silence for his R windup, and you out-trade and out-scale him at every stage past level 3.
edits.after: This only gets more lopsided. Malphite builds full armour while every tool you own — Rupture, Feral Scream, Vorpal Spikes — deals magic damage that armour never touches, and Feast's true damage deletes him however tanky he gets. Just remember the armour still feeds Ground Slam, whose damage scales off it. The one thing to respect all game is Unstoppable Force, 130s at rank 1, flanking your carries; in the side-lane 1v1 he cannot win. Keep stacking Feast and hold the silence for his R.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/malphite__chogath.json already flagged this level chart as contradicting the prose and explicitly said it could not propose the fix because it believed side/win were length-blocked. They are enum fields and exempt, so the flip is proposed here. One residual disagreement with the mirror, flagged in questionsForUser: their whys[3] rewrite claims Levels 4-5 as Malphite's best stretch, while the packet chart, the 55.62% headline over 1086 games and Cho'Gath's own whys[3] all give 4-5 to Cho'Gath. I followed the packet. UNVERIFIED: the mirror states Rupture's knockup stops Unstoppable Force, and _missing/chogath.json says the same thing — but the latter is derived from the 'grounding' flag on Rupture, which contradicts Riot's description (pop into the air and slow, no grounding). A knockup interrupting a dash mid-flight is ordinary League behaviour and I kept the mirror's phrasing rather than introduce a contradiction, but it is not confirmed by any file I read. The packet suspectName 'His Seismic Shard' is a false positive — the page has the name right.
